objections: The keyed token gives no real protection: stops.stop_id is tokenised with the same dataset-scope key, and the stops table carries exact lat/lon, so a token joins straight back to the exact boarding location. Disclosure is effectively the same as keep, contrary to the rationale.

Merging low-traffic stops (fewer than 10 taps) pools the rarely used stops that most narrowly point to a home (first boarding of the day) while keeping common stops for mode-choice analysis; stops.stop_id would then need raw or consistently merged ids so the join still works.
